races.name: Ladies Day Sunday 16th August Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Front-running style suits but stamina doubts over 3m½f and 278 days absence are concerns despite tactical advantage
runners_data.spotlight: In good form for Alison Thorpe in early part of last season, notably when winning at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good); yet fully to convince stamina-wise at around 3m and has fitness to prove on this stable debut (same owners) but Sean Bowen (who has won on him before) is booked; swaps visor for first-time blinkers.

runners_data.name: Anytrixwilldo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in retained blinkers faces traffic danger with three others wanting similar position early
runners_data.spotlight: 1-15 over fences; runner-up twice in cheekpieces at Ludlow (3m, good to soft) at start of this year but didn't fire in first-time blinkers (retained) at Fontwell last month; others are more persuasive.

runners_data.name: No More No
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfect for this pace shape but 393-day layoff is significant despite previous course form
runners_data.spotlight: Won over hurdles here in October 2024 and returned from seven-month break with wide-margin C&D (good) success on chasing debut last May; absent for another 13 months since and now 13lb higher but remains unexposed over fences and can evidently go well when fresh.

runners_data.name: Another Mystery
runners_data.note: Prominent style risky in this congested field but recent Fakenham win came against weak opposition
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to racing under rules with win in four-runner chase at Fakenham (3m, good) in April, in which his three rivals toiled and were pulled up; it's hard to gauge what that form is worth and his overall profile is not compelling but he clocked a good time (despite being eased right down).

runners_data.name: Wings On Wheels
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner benefits from pace setup but cheekpieces debut form at Huntingdon was modest
runners_data.spotlight: Still unexposed under rules and was seemingly aided by new cheekpieces when second of four at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in March; that form isn't anything to get excited about, though, and he was well held when third at Perth (2m4f, good to soft) last month; needs improvement over this new trip.

runners_data.name: Pleasure Garden
runners_data.note: Prominent style faces traffic issues and is 7lb higher in weights than recent Huntingdon fourth
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well for a long way before fading into fourth at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) last month but is effectively 7lb higher from out of the weights here and it's over three years since his only chase win; tries a new trip.

runners_data.name: Friends Don't Ask
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner has recent form but age and style profile work against him here
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time chase winner; no longer the force of old but returned from break with three placed runs last month, losing out only by a short head at Fontwell (3m2f, good) last time; can make his presence felt again.

runners_data.name: Milan Milos
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits race shape and tongue-tie proved effective at Plumpton winning debut over fences
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 over hurdles but battled on well to make winning chase debut in four-runner contest at Plumpton (3m1f, good; first-time tongue-tie) in April and was nudged up only 2lb for that; remains unexposed beyond 2m4f; no surprise if he features.

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who races too freely but showed improvement when stepped up to 3m at Bangor
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who tends to race too freely but displayed considerable improvement when upped to 3m and switched to fences at Bangor (good) in April, winning by 5l; beaten about 21l when second over C&D last month but gave the all-the-way winner far too much rope that day, and his margin of defeat was magnified by late jumping errors; remains of strong interest.

races.paceDynamic: Limerick Leader will take them along at a steady gallop from the front, with four prominent runners (Anytrixwilldo, Another Mystery, Pleasure Garden, Friends Don't Ask) creating congestion behind him in the early stages. This cluster will create traffic problems turning for home, particularly affecting those needing room. With five hold-up horses (No More No, Wings On Wheels, Milan Milos, Huckleberry Sting) at the back, the pace will be solid but not frantic through the middle sections. This race shape strongly favours the front-running Limerick Leader and hold-up horses who can avoid the prominent traffic jam.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Limerick Leader gets an uncontested lead and maintains his jumping rhythm
scenarios.body: The sustained pace over 3m½f will stretch the field and expose stamina doubts in several runners. His 278-day break becomes irrelevant as the tactical advantage proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group gets into a pace battle 3-4 out creating stoppage
scenarios.body: The backmarkers find clear runs while the prominent runners compromise each other in traffic. No More No's class and Milan Milos's finishing kick benefit from the setup.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner escapes the traffic and maintains position throughout
scenarios.body: Anytrixwilldo or Another Mystery avoid the congestion and track Limerick Leader without pressure. Their proximity to the pace becomes an asset when the leader's stamina questions surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Limerick Leader stops suddenly and the prominent group stalls in traffic
scenarios.body: A complete reshuffling occurs in the final half-mile as the race falls apart tactically. An outsider from midfield or a hold-up horse with the best finishing kick capitalizes on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch for early crowding as Anytrixwilldo, Another Mystery, Pleasure Garden and Friends Don't Ask all want prominent positions behind Limerick Leader
Monitor Limerick Leader's jumping rhythm early - if he makes mistakes the traffic behind could cause carnage
Watch how Milan Milos settles early given his tendency to be keen, as his hold-up style depends on relaxing
Check if No More No shows any ring-rustiness early after 393 days off despite his obvious class advantage
Observe Huckleberry Sting's position turning in - his free-running style could leave him with too much to do from the back

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Electric Eddy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner suited by sustainable pace, but pulled up on penultimate start raises reliability concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on well for second on chase debut at Hereford (2m, good) in November but was pulled up on next outing and made low-key reappearance when third of five (probably only fourth best on merit) at Worcester (2m, good) last month; needs to up his game here.

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Natural leader who found ideal conditions at Market Rasen, but 12th failed chase attempt before that win highlights inconsistency
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who was left clear just after final fence to score at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) in April, opening his chase account at the 12th attempt, but needs to bounce back quickly from a poor run there 12 days ago.

runners_data.name: Alshadhian
runners_data.note: Last year's impressive winner returns after eight-month break with major fitness question despite retaining ability
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race by 13l a year ago and was still in good form when last seen last summer/autumn; has fitness to prove after eight-month absence, though, and current mark probably demands a career-best performance.

runners_data.name: Kill The Groove
runners_data.note: Prominent style fits race shape but 9lb drop reflects poor recent chase form and cheekpieces failed last time
runners_data.spotlight: Now 9lb lower than when going close over hurdles at Plumpton (2m, soft) in January but was safely held in both chases this spring (2m3f/2m), and cheekpieces didn't appear to help much when used once previously.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Fast-improving chaser with excellent Skelton 14-day record (14/27), tongue-tie retained after easy Worcester debut win six days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Fast-improving mare who won easily on chasing debut at Worcester (2m, good; first-time tongue-tie) 12 days ago and has quickly added two easy hurdle wins (2m4f/2m, good) to her tally; probably still a long way ahead of the handicapper and can continue her winning spree here.

runners_data.name: Walk The Plank
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage in likely steadily-run race, needs tempo lift to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: Battled well for narrow success at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March, his third chase start, and gave another good account before fading into fourth at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) 12 days ago; might collect a minor prize.

runners_data.name: Fond Farewell
runners_data.note: Rearward position and poor hurdle form make this a significant step up, tongue-tie fitted for first time
runners_data.spotlight: Won a low-grade Flat handicap in Ireland in 2023 but unplaced all six hurdle runs for current stable; not beaten far when fifth of six at Worcester (2m, good) recently but not bred for chasing; others are much safer.

races.paceDynamic: Catchim is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the start, likely setting a sustainable gallop without pressure from other pace angles. Electric Eddy, Alshadhian, Kill The Groove and Beorma will all track prominently behind the leader, creating a bunched field through the middle stages. Walk The Plank and Fond Farewell will need to come from off the pace but face the challenge of making up ground in a race likely to be run at a modest tempo. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can position close enough to strike when Catchim's stamina gives way, rather than hold-up horses facing a tough task from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Catchim Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Catchim maintains his galloping rhythm and jumps cleanly throughout the two miles
scenarios.body: The leader's recent Market Rasen success shows he can sustain his effort when not pressured early, and with no other natural pace-setters he can dictate ideal fractions. Electric Eddy and Beorma are best placed to respond if he falters late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Tells
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners bunch up and increase the tempo from halfway
scenarios.body: Electric Eddy and Alshadhian have the class to benefit from a stronger gallop that will expose Catchim's stamina limitations over this trip. Beorma's recent fast-improving form makes her dangerous if the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the early stages creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Walk The Plank showed battling qualities when winning at Huntingdon and could benefit from a slow-run race that plays to his finishing kick. The modest early pace would allow back-markers to close the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Alshadhian Returns Refreshed
scenarios.trigger: If the defending champion shows no ill-effects from his 236-day layoff
scenarios.body: His 13-length victory in this race last year demonstrates his effectiveness at the track and trip, and the long absence could have reinvigorated him. The prominent style that served him well previously remains intact.

watchPoints.text: Beorma quick turnaround from six days ago could catch up with her despite Dan Skelton's excellent strike-rate with recent winners
Catchim's jumping under pressure given his poor chase record before Market Rasen breakthrough
Alshadhian for any signs of ring-rustiness in paddock or early stages after 236-day absence
Electric Eddy for any reluctance to race given pulled-up effort two starts ago
Walk The Plank's early positioning as hold-up horse needs to stay closer than usual in likely modest pace

races.name: Southwell Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Nazare
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who lost his way after November hurdles wins and was disappointing favorite last time, faces pace disadvantage here
runners_data.spotlight: Lost his way after winning twice over hurdles in November (2m4f, good to soft; once here) and was a disappointing favourite when well-held third of four on last month's chasing debut at Ludlow (3m, good); may yet turn things around but comes here with quite a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Manowest
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making chase debut for in-form Olly Murphy, has workable mark but poor recent hurdles form and 27 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Just 1-12 over hurdles and ran poorly when upped to 3m2f at Perth last month; makes chasing debut from a workable mark, though, and his Irish point win in 2024 bodes well for his prospects over fences.

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with February hat-trick form, returns after 53-day break but controls pace in small field
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form and completed quick hat-trick over hurdles in February (2m-2m4f, good to soft/soft) but quickly went off the boil towards end of last season (pulled up on two of last three appearances); competes off his lower chase mark here and might be allowed an uncontested lead but has a poor completion rate over fences; risky.

runners_data.name: Cher Monsieur
runners_data.note: Forward-going type with recent chase win at Plumpton, race-fit advantage on 14-day turnaround with top-trainer combo
runners_data.spotlight: Scored over hurdles at start of this year and built upon his promising chase debut when winning four-runner race at Plumpton (2m4f, good) a fortnight ago; only 3lb higher here and probably still on the upgrade; wears tongue-tie for first time; good chance.

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Blue will dictate terms from the front with his confirmed leading style, setting a steady tempo over this 2m4½f trip without pressure from pace rivals. Cher Monsieur may track prominently from his forward position, while hold-up horses Nazare and Manowest will settle towards the rear in this small field. The sustainable early gallop will set up a tactical finish where positioning and stamina become crucial. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and strike late, as the patient hold-up horses may struggle to make up ground against the solid tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Cher Monsieur tracks Thank You Blue closely and times his challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: The improving chaser can use his forward position to pressure the leader turning in, benefiting from recent race fitness and momentum from his Plumpton success. His prominent style perfectly suits tracking the honest gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds Gamely
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Blue maintains his rhythm and repels late challenges
scenarios.body: The hat-trick winner's front-running style encounters no early pressure, allowing him to control the race and kick clear when others come under pressure. His proven stamina at this trip gives him the edge in a staying battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong and the leaders tire
scenarios.body: Nazare or Manowest could benefit from a collapse up front, using their patient tactics to sweep past weakening rivals in the final furlong. The hold-up style would capitalize on others going too fast too soon.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Blue goes too fast early under pressure from Cher Monsieur
scenarios.body: Both prominent runners could empty out in the straight, leaving the door open for the patient hold-up horses to pick up the pieces late. This tactical meltdown would completely reverse the expected race shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch how closely Cher Monsieur tracks Thank You Blue early, as their battle will determine the race tempo
Monitor if Thank You Blue shows any rustiness after his 53-day layoff when asked to quicken
Observe whether Nazare or Manowest can get into contention at the second-last, as both need everything to fall right from hold-up positions
Check if Manowest handles fences better than his hurdles form suggests on his chasing debut
Watch for any tactical errors from the inexperienced chase riders in this small but competitive field

races.name: Ladies Day Sunday 16th August Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Trigger The Light
runners_data.note: Front-running style but long absence of 221 days since last run creates fitness doubts despite trainer booking claiming jockey
runners_data.spotlight: Made quite promising rules debut when third in seven-runner Warwick bumper (good) in October but was pulled up on hurdling debut later that month (2m4f, good to soft); had wind op during seven-month break.

runners_data.name: Run Happy
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but inexperienced with only one rules start and needs to improve significantly from Aintree fifth
runners_data.spotlight: Made quite promising rules debut when fifth of 14 in pointers' bumper at Aintree (good) last month but almost certainly needs to improve to threaten the principals on this hurdling debut.

runners_data.name: Manalishi
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suits expected pace scenario and consistent placed form shows reliable level of ability
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up on last year's bumper debut and placed on all three hurdling starts, most recently when clear second of eight at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last month; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Hawk's Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent style with Irish raider showing promise in cheekpieces and recent Cartmel fourth suggests upward trajectory
runners_data.spotlight: Irish raider who launched hurdling career with two promising runs in cheekpieces last month, latterly when close fourth of ten at Cartmel (2m6f, good); that form already puts him on the premises here, and he can improve if he cuts out the jumping errors.

runners_data.name: Who's Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with useful Flat background and strong hurdling record for McCain including Musselburgh series final third
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat racer who made the frame on four of his five hurdling starts for Donald McCain last season, most notably when third in valuable series final at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) in March; well beaten in good-quality Flat handicap last month but ought to play a significant role in this.

runners_data.name: Rock Sensation
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won course bumper for different trainer but disappointing hurdling form since stable switch
runners_data.spotlight: Won good-ground course bumper for Ben Pauling in spring 2025 and made the frame in soft-ground Listed bumper at Cheltenham in November but has made an underwhelming start to her hurdling career; shaped with some promise on last month's stable debut at Fontwell (2m1f, good) but was safely held in the end; needs to up her game over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Papillondelumiere
runners_data.note: Prominent style but poor hurdling form as 100-1 shot suggests limited ability despite pointing background
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden pointer who was soundly beaten when 100-1 for first two hurdling starts.

runners_data.name: Granite Sands
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing gradual improvement and recent Stratford third suggests capable of better with step forward
runners_data.spotlight: Bettered low-key hurdle debut when keeping on for modest third of six at Stratford (2m6f, good to firm) last month but needs to take another good step forward here.

runners_data.name: Jacquette
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but poor recent form and trainer switch suggests struggling to find competitive level
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at huge odds on both hurdling starts for Danni O'Neill; now with Georgie Howell.

races.paceDynamic: Trigger The Light will set a sustainable pace from the front with Run Happy, Hawk's Rock, and Papillondelumiere tracking prominently in the early stages. The lack of confirmed speed horses means the gallop will be steady rather than searching, allowing the hold-up brigade including Manalishi, Who's Glen, Rock Sensation, Granite Sands, and Jacquette to stay in touch throughout. The race will develop into a tactical affair over the final 4f with plenty in contention turning for home. This moderate early pace strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce their best work late, particularly those with proven finishing kicks like Manalishi and Who's Glen.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate throughout and several runners are in contention at the last
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of the hold-up brigade pay dividends as they sweep past tiring leaders in the final furlong. Manalishi and Who's Glen have the class and finishing speed to capitalize on this setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Hawk's Rock or Run Happy can secure ideal positions behind the leaders
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners gets first run on the field and maintains their advantage to the line. Their tactical positioning allows them to strike at the right moment without facing a wall of late closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Trigger The Light faces no early pressure and dictates throughout
scenarios.body: The leader gets an uncontested lead and maintains enough in reserve to hold off late challengers. The lack of early pace pressure allows sustainable fractions that favor the horse on the engine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the favorites get caught up in traffic or tactical battles
scenarios.body: The pace scenario creates opportunities for a lesser-fancied runner to slip through and capitalize on others' misfortune. Granite Sands or Rock Sensation could profit from a perfectly judged ride.

watchPoints.text: Trigger The Light's 221-day absence could see fitness lacking in closing stages despite taking them there
Hawk's Rock racing in cheekpieces for second time after promising debut in headgear suggests trainer expects improvement
Who's Glen returning from 69-day break with 32 days on Flat suggests freshness but potential for rustiness early
Run Happy stepping up significantly in class from Aintree pointers' bumper to face experienced hurdlers
Manalishi's consistent placed form makes any drift in betting significant given reliable level of ability

races.name: Vaughandale Construction 'Built To Last' Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Phantom Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 25-day break with previous bumper win suggesting ability, but lacks recent competitive hurdles form
runners_data.spotlight: Did not get competitive in three maiden/novice hurdles (2m-2m4f) for new stable this spring, following a long absence, but won a bumper by 9l in summer 2023 and there's still a chance some of that ability will resurface at some point; watch the betting.

runners_data.name: Collanisi
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid third last time and strong trainer form, looks progressive in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Made solid start to handicap career when close third of eight at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last month and any improvement on that performance will give him a good shout here.

runners_data.name: Paragon
runners_data.note: Forward-going type wearing cheekpieces, recent Market Rasen fourth gives him solid form edge
runners_data.spotlight: Made fairly encouraging handicap debut over C&D (good) last month and his recent fourth in first-time cheekpieces at Market Rasen (2m, good) was also respectable; needs to find something extra today, though.

runners_data.name: Global Hideaway
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter returning after 357 days off with bleeding concerns, but new stable could rejuvenate
runners_data.spotlight: Bled from the nose on final two starts for Dan Skelton, latterly when pulled-up 66-1 shot on handicap debut just under a year ago; now with Christian Williams (same owner); others have much less to prove.

runners_data.name: Caspada
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with scope after Chepstow second, but 46-day break may hinder fitness levels
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on first two hurdling starts but belied 150-1 odds when second in 14-runner Chepstow maiden (2m, good) in April and has plenty of scope for further improvement in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Brooklyn Lullaby
runners_data.note: Hold-up type making handicap debut after 255-day absence, major fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no significant promise when a big-priced outsider for three maiden hurdles last August/September and makes handicap debut after a 255-day absence; 2lb wrong; of interest only if attracting market support.

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent winning form, French background suggests tactical speed available
runners_data.spotlight: Made low-key start to British hurdling career last season but delivered on promise shown on the Flat in France when winning from off the pace on last month's handicap hurdle debut at Stratford (2m, good to firm); could easily have more improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who showed frame form in spring but refused to race on Flat, consistency concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed promise when making the frame in two maiden hurdles (2m, good/good to firm) this spring but he refused to race on the Flat in between and needs to improve to overcome top weight on this handicap hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare now 0-15 over hurdles despite recent Market Rasen effort, profile looks limited
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced when fifth of seven (behind Paragon) at Market Rasen (2m, good) 12 days ago, after a break, but is now 0-15 over hurdles and her overall profile is not appealing.

runners_data.name: Beaufort Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 524 days with fading tendencies, massive fitness question
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner in spring 2024; well beaten at triple-digit odds in three novice/maiden hurdles in 2024-25 season (2m-2m4f) but two of those were good-quality races at Cheltenham; makes handicap debut after a long absence but remains unexposed and is worth a glance in the betting.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who races too freely, soundly beaten in recent handicap debut over course and distance
runners_data.spotlight: Unable to justify prominence in the betting when soundly beaten in first two handicaps, the latter over C&D last month, and his tendency to race too freely remains a worry; evidently thought capable of better, though.

races.paceDynamic: Global Hideaway is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms without early pressure in this 11-runner field. The prominent runners Collanisi and Paragon will likely track him in the early stages, but with eight hold-up horses in the field, the majority will settle towards the rear. Global Hideaway can set a comfortable rhythm through the early stages before the race develops into a proper test from the final hurdle. This sustainable pace setup strongly favours the hold-up horses who can finish late, particularly those with proven tactical speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Global Hideaway sets uncontested fractions and the field comes to him late
scenarios.body: The patient rides get the ideal setup to unleash finishing kicks, with the large pack of hold-up horses creating a cavalry charge finish. Those with the best tactical speed and race fitness will prevail over the tiring pace-setter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front End Holds Firm
scenarios.trigger: If Global Hideaway maintains his kick and the prominent runners stay close enough
scenarios.body: The early leaders resist the late charge by maintaining strong galloping rhythm, with Collanisi and Paragon benefiting from their forward positions. The hold-up horses leave their runs too late on the sustained pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test over the final two furlongs, suiting horses with natural pace regardless of running style. Versatile and Prettylady can quicken best when the race falls apart tactically.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If Global Hideaway goes too fast early or multiple horses challenge for the lead
scenarios.body: Early pace becomes unsustainable with horses getting into a speed battle, setting up the race for a complete outsider to pick up the pieces. The unconsidered hold-up horses benefit from the collapse.

watchPoints.text: Global Hideaway could stop quickly if bleeding problems resurface after his long absence
Littletown Lad may race too keenly again and compromise his finishing kick like in recent starts
Brooklyn Lullaby and Beaufort Breeze face severe fitness tests after 255 and 524-day breaks respectively
Collanisi and Paragon both hold strong recent form and will likely be prominent throughout
Prettylady's winning form last time makes her the hold-up horse to beat if the pace sets up right

races.name: Free Racenight Thursday 18th June Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Callin Baton Rouge
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tough task with limited pace pressure, though trip increase and 2lb drop in weights are positives for this 8-year-old mare
runners_data.spotlight: Not quite at her best this year but has dropped another 2lb since last month's respectable third at Huntingdon (2m, good to firm) and this move back up in trip won't be a problem; probably won't be far away.

runners_data.name: William Of York
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with poor recent completion rate but Charlie Maggs(3) claim helps offset the 10-year-old's regression over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Regressive 10yo who has poor completion rate over fences since returning from layoff in November; stopped the rot with fairly respectable hurdle run last month but needs to build on that performance here; swaps visor for refitted cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Achille Des Rocs
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but 65-day layoff concerning after disappointing chase return, though Brian Hughes booking is significant positive
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner (2m/2m3f, good) towards end of 2024; not yet fully exposed but returned from one-year absence with disappointing chase run in April and needs to get career back on track.

runners_data.name: Golden Glance
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse out of form since wind operation but Aintree effort last time showed signs of improvement returning
runners_data.spotlight: Out of form since returning from long absence in December, albeit her seventh of eight at Aintree (2m4f, good; first run after wind op) last month was arguably more encouraging than bare form suggests; others have more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Fighting Falcon
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with tactical advantage but warning signs about fading in finish could be crucial over this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who made winning stable debut when back under rules at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good; first-time cheekpieces) last month; drew well clear of the others with the runner-up there and could still be well treated after a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner gets significant weight relief at 145lbs but recent fall and inconsistent jumping record raises reliability questions
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from break with low-key chase run last month and fell mid-race when back over hurdles nine days ago but remains on a good mark and will be suited by today's trip/ground; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: Prominent runner without win since December 2023 but consistent place record and good course history keep him competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Without a win since December 2023 but lost out only by a nose at Worcester (2m4f, good) last summer and returned from break with satisfactory run at Fontwell last month; contender if that recent outing brought him on.

runners_data.name: Ruler Legend
runners_data.note: Prominent style ideally suited to race shape with strong recent form including two Market Rasen wins showing he handles this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season in excellent form, winning twice at Market Rasen (2m/2m2f, good), and his second at Market Rasen (2m, good) 12 days ago was another good effort; should be fine over this longer trip; respected.

races.paceDynamic: Fighting Falcon is the only confirmed front runner and should set a comfortable tempo without pressure through the early stages. With William Of York, Achille Des Rocs, Royal Rhythm and Ruler Legend likely to track in prominent positions, the pace should be sustainable rather than frantic over this 2m4½f trip. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the leaders can dictate terms, while hold-up horses like Callin Baton Rouge, Golden Glance and Gone In Sixty will need the tempo to collapse late to be effective. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners who can sit close to Fighting Falcon and have first strike when the race develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Fighting Falcon sets steady fractions and the prominent horses get first run
scenarios.body: The comfortable pace allows trackers to conserve energy before pouncing, while hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on leaders who haven't been softened up. Achille Des Rocs and Ruler Legend are perfectly positioned to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Fighting Falcon maintains his recent front-running form and the pace stays honest
scenarios.body: The 5-year-old's low mileage and recent Uttoxeter victory suggest he can sustain his effort better than older rivals, especially with comfortable fractions early. His trainer Stuart Edmunds is in good form and the step up in trip suits his style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong or Fighting Falcon stops quickly as warned
scenarios.body: Gone In Sixty's light weight advantage becomes crucial in a truly-run race, while Callin Baton Rouge's class tells when given a proper test of stamina. Both need maximum assistance from pace scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upset Special
scenarios.trigger: If the principals underperform or track conditions deteriorate significantly
scenarios.body: Golden Glance's Aintree run was better than it looked and wind surgery may have helped, while any of the longer shots could benefit from a messy pace collapse. Requires multiple favourite failures.

watchPoints.text: Fighting Falcon's tendency to fade in the finish could be exposed over this longer 2m4½f trip despite his front-running advantage
Achille Des Rocs making his first start for 65 days after disappointing chase return - market support will indicate connections' confidence
Gone In Sixty's jumping reliability after recent fall, especially given his hold-up style requires clean jumps to maintain position
William Of York's completion rate given his poor record over fences since November, though hurdles may suit better
Golden Glance's response to wind surgery becoming apparent if pace develops into proper test of stamina

races.name: Celebrate With Sponsorship At Southwell Racecourse Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Artiste d'Ainay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 21-day break with modest recent hurdles form after point-to-point success
runners_data.spotlight: Easily made all in a point in April but was just a respectable fifth over hurdles at Hexham (2m7f, good) for new connections last month and needs to build on that performance here.

runners_data.name: Copper Beach
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with two seconds last month, tongue-tie addition and step up in trip should suit
runners_data.spotlight: Came from off the pace to take second twice last month (2m4f/2m3f, good; tongue-tie added), after a long layoff, and is likely to be suited by this move back up in trip; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Danger Nap
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with unexposed potential at 3m+, cheekpieces first time last start when clear second
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 5yo who was clear second when upped to 3m1f and fitted with first-time cheekpieces for last month's handicap debut at Warwick (good); could still have more to offer; high on the list.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: Prominent type but pulled up last time and Flat breeding raises stamina doubts over this extended trip
runners_data.spotlight: Ran okay when third of five at Fontwell (2m1f, good to soft) in April but was pulled up on latest outing, and his Flat pedigree raises doubts about the suitability of this new trip; swaps cheekpieces for refitted visor.

runners_data.name: East Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with career-best 9-length win at Stratford 3m2f, proven at this distance
runners_data.spotlight: Showed career-best form when scoring by 9l at Stratford (3m2f, good) in April and also has a C&D success on his CV but was unable to land a telling blow on his two starts at Hexham last month and needs to kick on again to overcome current mark.

runners_data.name: Iamcelestialgift
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 151-day break with mixed handicap record and plenty to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Won on hurdling debut in April 2025 (2m3f) but struggled in both handicaps last season (3m/2m5f); returns from five-month break with a lot to prove.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with C&D win on CV, entitled to improve after reappearance run 33 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice last year on good ground (once over C&D) and is entitled to have benefited from last month's reappearance run but may find others in this field better handicapped.

runners_data.name: Getaway Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse out of form since wind operation, first-time visor replaces cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Out of form (mainly over fences) since returning from long absence in January (had wind op before latest run); swaps cheekpieces for first-time visor and has tongue-tie refitted; revival needed.

runners_data.name: Fairly Fulling
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who broke maiden duck at 14th attempt, pulled up when dropped to 2m last time
runners_data.spotlight: Came good over hurdles at 14th attempt, with clear success at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in March, but ran poorly when dropped back to 2m last month and it's hard to know what to expect from him on first attempt at 3m under rules.

runners_data.name: Can U Feel It
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing improvement with tongue-tie addition, third at Fakenham last time
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over hurdles but put in good front-running shift when third at Fakenham (2m4f, good; first-time tongue-tie) last month and is open to more improvement over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: L'Air du Large
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 169-day break with poor recent handicap form
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed after only five hurdle runs but struggled in first two handicaps (2m/2m3f; cheekpieces added last time); upped in trip again for first run since December; considered only if lively in the betting.

runners_data.name: Stripe Of Honour
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with C&D win last October but major fitness concerns after 250-day absence
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who was in good form in the early part of last season and gained a narrow C&D (good) win on latest outing in October; only 3lb higher today but has fitness to prove and younger rivals appeal more.

runners_data.name: Porridge
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with poor record but hiked up in weights after one good fourth at Fontwell
runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 over hurdles; excelled herself when fourth at huge odds in 2m3f Fontwell maiden in April but, having been hiked up the weights, was soundly beaten in both subsequent handicaps (2m5f/2m7f).

races.paceDynamic: Danger Nap will take them along from the front with minimal pressure, as the field lacks confirmed early pace. The prominent group of Artiste d'Ainay, Copper Beach, Ikigai Star, and Iamcelestialgift will track the leader but none are natural pace pressers. With most runners holding back early, the tempo will be steady rather than fierce through the long middle section of this 3m½f test. This controlled pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce sustained finishes, as they'll have plenty left in the tank when the real racing begins turning for home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Danger Nap sets uncontested fractions and the field remains patient
scenarios.body: The steady gallop allows hold-up horses to conserve energy for telling late surges over the final half-mile. East Eagle, Indian Sunbird, and Can U Feel It are perfectly positioned to unleash finishing kicks when it matters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Running Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Danger Nap maintains momentum and the chasers fail to close
scenarios.body: The leader's class advantage tells as pursuing horses struggle to reel him in over the extended trip. His recent 3m1f second at Warwick suggests he can see out this longer distance when allowed his own way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Press
scenarios.trigger: If Copper Beach or Ikigai Star apply early pressure to Danger Nap
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates gaps for the handiest horses positioned just behind the pace. Runners tracking in fourth or fifth can pick off tired leaders while avoiding the worst of any early speed duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Staying Test Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses struggle with the trip as the pace quickens late
scenarios.body: The extended distance finds out several runners' stamina limitations in the final furlong. Only the most genuine stayers with proven form over similar trips can sustain their effort to the line.

watchPoints.text: Danger Nap's jumping under pressure - any mistakes could hand initiative to closers in straight
Copper Beach's stamina over this extended trip - only raced up to 2m6f previously
East Eagle's ability to reproduce Stratford form with 3lb claimer Maggs taking over riding duties
Iamcelestialgift's fitness after five-month layoff - market support would indicate readiness
Indian Sunbird's position turning for home - needs to be within striking distance to use proven finishing kick
